title: Neighborhood home-cooking marketplace
adjacent_why: Same shape as 01 — same city, same buildings, same verified-neighbor trust ritual, same take-rate split, same waived liability. Different actors and a different hinge: a perishable handoff window and an unpermitted kitchen, not an unsupervised animal.
idea: A mobile marketplace where residents of the same apartment complex order home-cooked lunch boxes from verified neighbors who cook in their own kitchens. Cooks keep 85% of the order value; the platform takes 15%. Trust is built via government ID, a kitchen photo tour, and the first three orders free for new cooks. Handoff happens in the lobby between cook and buyer — no couriers, no cold chain, and no food-handling permit is asked for at signup. Orders close at 10am for a 12pm pickup window, and one cook usually carries a whole tower. Launch city is Jakarta high-rises only.
focus_notes: Foodborne illness with no permit, no insurance and a waived liability clause
One cook per tower — supply concentration inside a single building
Perishable pickup window: a missed 12pm handoff is unrecoverable, not rescheduled
Repeat orders move to a WhatsApp group once buyer and cook have met
